key_insight: A single flexible fiber in a microfluidic channel can become a bistable “fluidic hysteron” through nonlinear flow–structure feedback, enabling memory, hysteresis, and avalanche-like switching in flow networks.
engineering_relevance: This provides a passive, geometry-tunable way to encode and control memory in microfluidic systems, with potential uses in adaptive fluidic logic, sensing, and programmable flow routing.
method: Anchor an elastic fiber in a microfluidic channel so viscous loading deforms it.
Exploit deformation-induced changes in hydraulic resistance and flow redistribution to create bistability.
Use bypass-channel geometry to tune load-line effects and interactions across fiber arrays.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a cusp-catastrophe onset for a single fiber and a geometry-driven transition in arrays from noninteracting Preisach behavior with return-point memory to interacting avalanching behavior with return-point memory violation.
watch_item: Bistability and memory depend strongly on channel geometry and hydraulic coupling, so small fabrication variations could shift or eliminate the intended switching behavior.
paper_title: Fluidic hysterons and memory in flow networks
